title: JPEG, PNG or WebP? Choosing an Image Format
description: Compare JPEG, PNG and WebP for photos, graphics, transparency and web delivery, with practical checks before converting images.
intro: Image formats make different trade-offs. The best choice depends on the kind of image, whether transparency matters, the destination's support and the quality you need to preserve.

sections.heading: JPEG for many photographs
paragraphs: JPEG is widely supported and often works well for photographs. It uses lossy compression, so repeated edits and saves can accumulate visible artifacts. Keep a high-quality original and export a new copy for delivery.
JPEG does not preserve transparency. Transparent regions may become a solid background when converted.

sections.heading: PNG for transparency and sharp edges
paragraphs: PNG is useful for transparency, interface elements, logos and graphics with sharp edges. It is lossless, but photographic PNG files can be considerably larger than a compressed photo format.
For a photo with transparency, check whether the destination accepts PNG or another alpha-capable format before converting.

sections.heading: WebP for supported web workflows
paragraphs: WebP supports lossy and lossless encoding, as well as transparency. It can be efficient for web use, but verify that your content system, image pipeline and receiving application accept it.
There is no universal rule that WebP is always smaller. Compare the output files at an acceptable visual quality for the particular image.

sections.heading: Convert and compare
paragraphs: Use the Image Format Converter to convert among supported image types. Review transparency, colour, edges and file size after conversion. To reduce bytes while keeping the same format, the Image Compressor may be a better fit.
Do not overwrite the only original. Keep a source copy so you can export again with different settings if the destination rejects the result.

faq.question: Which format is best for photos?
faq.answer: JPEG is broadly compatible; WebP may be more efficient when supported. Compare quality and size for the actual image.

faq.question: Which format supports transparent backgrounds?
faq.answer: PNG and WebP can support transparency. JPEG does not.

faq.question: Will converting JPEG to PNG restore lost detail?
faq.answer: No. Conversion changes the container/encoding, not detail already lost in the JPEG source.

faq.question: Can I compress PNG without changing its format?
faq.answer: Yes, though the achievable reduction depends on image content and compression method. If transparency is not needed, compare other formats too.
